_note: ⛔ SNG-393. Named in an OLDER REGISTER at Erik's ruling — the settlement names are plain and functional (the Spent Yard, Thinwater, the Long Grey) because people named the places they work. ⚠️ SEAS AND RANGES ARE NOT WORKED. They were named before anyone was doing anything here, and the names weathered instead of being replaced. Archaic compounds, weathered vowels, no grandeur — the difference between a name a foreman gives a yard and a name that outlived the language it came from.
_derived: Every feature below was DETECTED from the terrain, not invented: seas are connected water over 300 cells; ranges are connected land above the 93rd elevation percentile, split range-vs-massif by extent ratio. The names are authored; the features are measured.

seas.name: The Ythmere
seas.why: The world ocean. ⛔ 'Yth' is the oldest surviving element in any name on this map and nobody can say what it meant — the Lattice-cities' own records begin already using it. What is left is the -mere: water. A word for the sea that has forgotten half of itself.

seas.name: The Hollowmere
seas.why: The great inland water below the Center, reaching toward Greenmarch. Named for what it is not: a hollow that filled. ⚠️ Valleyfolk still say 'gone to the Hollowmere' for a thing that will not come back.

seas.name: Stairwater
seas.why: The water under Stair Hollow, stepped in shelves down its western side. A plain name gone old — it was 'the stair water' and the space closed.

seas.name: The Wendmere
seas.why: Where the Wend's ground gives out. The Churnfolk name it for the turning, not the water.

ranges.name: The Gramarch
ranges.why: The great massif above the Somatic reaches, over the Cogitarium's shoulder. ⛔ 'Gram' is grief and 'march' is a border in a language nobody here speaks any more — so the Somatics translate it as 'the hard walking' and are not wrong.

ranges.name: The Hourstones
ranges.why: The high ground the Hourkeepers built the Drawn Hour and the Slow Hour beneath. They did not name it; it was named, and they kept the name, which is what they do with everything.

ranges.name: The Kindlespine
ranges.why: The long ridge running past Kindlerow toward the Disputed Zone. Forge-country: the range gave the town its fuel and its name and then took the name back.

ranges.name: The Drownspine
ranges.why: The ridge above the Sunken Choir. ⚠️ Named after the flood, not before — the only range on the map whose name records an event, and the event is the drowning it failed to prevent.

ranges.name: The Rootwall
ranges.why: The northern range walling the Blocklands from the Slow Orchard. The Rootkin call it a wall and mean it kindly.

ranges.name: The Heartcrag
ranges.why: The high stone at the Heartroot's shoulder, where the life pole's ground turns to rock and stops.

ranges.name: The Wornheight
ranges.why: Above the Worn Yard and Greyhearth. Worn is the older word and the yard took it from the hill.

ranges.name: The Marchhead
ranges.why: The high ground between the Middle Way and the Marchward — a border's head, held by nobody, which is why both name it.

ranges.name: The Grallochstone
ranges.why: The one thing in Unspooling that has not moved. ⚠️ The Churnfolk find that funny and visit it.

ranges.name: The Underhorn
ranges.why: Above the Slow Stair and the Lampless Market — the last high stone before the ways go down. You see it, then you do not see anything for a long while.

ranges.name: The Figurehorn
ranges.why: A jointed peak above the Figure-Works, regular enough that the Figurists claim it and honest enough that it was there first.

ranges.name: The Lesser Horn
ranges.why: The smaller of the two above the Figure-Works. ⚠️ Named by comparison, which is the plainest thing on this list and the only one that sounds like the settlements do.

_anchoring: ⛔ RIVERS AND FENS ARE ANCHORED TO LOCATIONS, NOT TO GEOMETRY. I flagged that naming them was risky because both derive from flow and shift when terrain regenerates. Erik ruled name them, and this is how that holds: each name binds to `nearHead` / `nearMouth` / `near` — STABLE location ids — not to a traced path. ⚠️ THE PIPELINE RE-ATTACHES A NAME TO WHATEVER FEATURE IS NEAREST ITS ANCHOR AFTER A REBUILD. The Echo still runs past Millbrook even when its exact course moves. A name bound to coordinates would be lost; a name bound to a place is not.

rivers.name: The Echo
rivers.why: ⛔ THE GREAT RIVER. It rises near the Hundred Markets and runs most of the way round the world before it ends near Kestrel's Roost. Echo River Crossing is named for it; Millbrook's wheels turn on it. ⚠️ It is the only named thing on the map that touches nearly every disposition, and it is water, which the Numinous consider significant and the Enginewrights consider a shipping lane.

rivers.name: The Greenwater
rivers.why: Runs from Greenforge down toward the Forge-Eternal. Green going into black — the growers' water arriving where the makers use it, which is most of the foothills economy in one river.

rivers.name: The Choirwater
rivers.why: Rises at the Sunken Choir and runs toward the Lensward. ⚠️ It is the water that did the drowning and nobody has renamed it.

rivers.name: The Axewater
rivers.why: ⛔ THE FIRST WATER. It rises within four degrees of the Crossing — the closest any river comes to the pole — and runs out past the Axis Gate. 'Axe' is the axis worn down by saying.

rivers.name: The Middle Run
rivers.why: The Somatics' water, from the Middle Way toward the Given Land. They swim it as training and consider that the whole of its purpose.

rivers.name: The Switchwater
rivers.why: Comes down the Old Switchback's mountain, the road and the river using the same cut. The road is older by name and younger by fact.

rivers.name: The Kindle Run
rivers.why: From the forge-country down to Plainstead's flat. Kindlerow quenches in it and Plainstead drinks downstream, which they have argued about for two hundred years.

rivers.name: The Burnwater
rivers.why: Off the Burnscar into the Deepwood. ⚠️ The Ents let it in, which is not nothing.

rivers.name: The Longshore Water
rivers.why: Longshore to Gearsflat — the waygate town's river, running to the salvage yards. Bridge-wrights at one end and people who take bridges apart at the other.

rivers.name: The Greenward Water
rivers.why: Out of the Quickwood's edge toward the Making. Rootkin water reaching maker country.

fens.name: The Millfen
fens.why: ⛔ THE LARGEST WETLAND IN THE WORLD, and Millbrook stands at its edge rather than in it. The valley's over-fertile ground going soft — abandoned soil-conditioning nanite doing to water what it did to the fields.

fens.name: The Burnfen
fens.why: Where the Burnscar's runoff pools. Wet ground on a scar, which the Ents find instructive.

fens.name: The Marchfen
fens.why: Below Greenmarch at the Quickwood's edge — the last soft ground before the canopy closes.

fens.name: The Echofen
fens.why: Where the Echo slows before the crossing. ⚠️ The bridge exists because the fen made fording impossible, which is the whole reason the town is there.

fens.name: The Quiet Fen
fens.why: Beside the Quiet House. Nobody raises a hand here either, for a different reason.

fens.name: The Gatefen
fens.why: Around the Axis Gate's approaches. Twelve roads leave the Crossing and several of them are wet for the first week.

fens.name: The Stiltfen
fens.why: ⛔ THE SOUTHERN MARSH. Greywater Stilts stands ON it — the town is built on poles because this is what the ground does here.

fens.name: The Terrace Fen
fens.why: Where the Harmonic Heights' lowest terrace meets standing water. The sonic civilisation's drainage, which they do not discuss.

fens.name: The Plateau Fen
fens.why: At the Radiant Plateau's foot. Light above and wet below, which the Radiants consider a complete description of the world.

fens.name: The Stairfen
fens.why: Below Stair Hollow, where the steps run out into ground that will not hold one.
